question:
A 33-year-old male with a history of seizures is evaluated in the emergency department following a fall
during building climbing. Two weeks prior, his physician prescribed a new medication to treat
symptoms of depression, fatigue, and insomnia. His girlfriend reports he has experienced emotional
instability for several months. In the past three days, he has displayed sleeplessness and has been
obsessively preparing to climb Mount Everest, despite having no prior climbing experience. He has
also spent his entire savings on mountaineering equipment. On examination, he shows bruising on his
right upper extremity, exhibits pressured speech, is easily distracted, and while alert, is not oriented to
place. Which medication most likely triggered these behavioral changes? Answer Choices: (A)
Mirtazapine (B) Venlafaxine (C) Lamotrigine (D) Lithium (E) Sertraline (F) Escitalopram (G) Bupropion
(H) Aripiprazole (I) Duloxetine (J) Fluoxetine
 A. Escitalopram
B. Lithium
C. Lamotrigine
D. Fluoxetine
E. Mirtazapine
F. Sertraline
G. Aripiprazole
H. Duloxetine
I. Bupropion
J. Venlafaxine
